 Section 3 (1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires    (zf) "misbranded food" means an article of food    (c) if the article contained in the package    ( i ) . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . o r i s n o t l a b e l l e d i n a c c o r d a n c e w i t h t h e   r e q u i r e m e n t s o f t h i s A c t o r r e g u l a t i o n s m a d e t h e r e u n d e r   or is in contravention thereof:

From the plain reading of above provision, it is evident that the sample  commodity which was packaged, was required to comply with the labelling  requirements as prescribed under FSS Act and FSS(P&L) Regulations.
Thus, the appellant's contention that the FSS (P&L) Regulations were not  applicable to the sample commodity, is untenable.

6.3 As far as the appellant's plea that the coconut milk was not being "sold" to  t h e c o n s u m e r , a s i t w a s s i m p l y t o b e u s e d a s a n  ingredient; and that he being only a distributor and had sold the sample  commodity in the same sealed condition as bought from the importer, he  is not liable, is concerned, let me refer to the definition of "sale" as laid  down in clause (zr) of Section 3 FSS Act, which reads under: " Section 3 (1) 
 I n t h i s A c t , u n l e s s t h e c o n t e x t o t h e r w i s e r e q u i r e s   (zr) "sale" with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, means the  s a l e o f a n y a r t i c l e o f f o o d , w h e t h e r f o r c a s h o r o n c r e d i t o r  b y w a y o f e x c h a n g e a n d w h e t h e r b y w h o l e s a l e  or retail, for human consumption or use, or for analysis, and includes an  agreement for sale, an offer for sale, the exposing for sale or having in possession  for sale of any such article, and includes also an attempt to sell any  such article
From the above, it is apparent that the 'Sale' includes whether by 'wholesale or  retail' of any "article of food" for "human consumption" or use.
As  noted above, coconut milk falls within the definition of 'food', which was meant for human  consumption.

In view of the above provision, even the FBO who distributes any food article is   duty bound to comply with the FSS Act and FSS (P&L) Regulations.
7.2 Even Section 27 makes it clear.

Section 27(2)(c) reads as under:
"27. Liability of Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.
(1) ....
( 2 ) T h e w h o l e s a l e r o r d i s t r i b u t o r s h a l l b e l i a b l e u n d e r  this Act for any article of food which is (a) ....
(b) ....
(c) unsafe or misbranded, or ..."
7.3 The sample of chakoh coconut milk lifted from the FBO has been found to be supplied by  the appellant.
The same has not been disputed by the appellant.
The appellant being  the distributor of the sample commodity was required to comply with the FSS Act and FSS  (P&L) Regulations.

9.0 The Ld. Counsel for the appellant subsequently pleaded that he does not press the above  p l e a s a n d p r a y e d f o r l e n i e n t v i e w a n d  reduction in quantum of penalty in view of the fact that the appellant is a senior citizen aged  a b o u t 7 0 y e a r s .

However, the Ld. ADM has imposed a penalty of only Rs.2 lacs.
Further, not indicating the product to be vegetarian/nonvegetarian and nonmentioning  of best before/expiry date, are serious matters.
Use of expired chakoh coconut milk could have  caused serious health concern to the consumer.
In view of these facts and circumstances and  considering the other violations, no ground for reduction of penalty is made out.
